courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: The component we'll use now allows us to pick a date. Ionic has a dedicated component that makes picking
dates pretty easy and that offers a lot of features and therefore, let's add that component now.
I'll add a new ion-row here and I'll add an ion-item with an ion-label because that date component
will work like a regular form input which is a really good thing and therefore we can use it together
with a label and so on and I'll set the title here to available from, so that users can define for
which timespan they want to offer their place
and now I will remove the ion-input and instead add the ion-datetime component here and that will give
us a nice date picker.
Now the cool thing is, there you can set a min and a max value and you can of course populate that
dynamically,
you could bind this with square brackets to any value you calculate in Typescript, for now I will just
bind it to a hardcoded values and you enter dates here in the ISO format and you'll find more about
that in the official Ionic docs, on the date time component and one valid input for example is a four-digit
year, then a dash, then the month, then the day.
So let's say we want to allow dates from January the 1st 2019 all the way up to December 31st
in 2022 and of course as I said, you could calculate this dynamically, you could also set a longer range
all the way to 25, whatever you want.
So now, this is my available from date time,
now I actually want to set the available to date time control next to this one and therefore, I'll change
the size here. On small devices,
this should have a width of 3, still have an offset of three because I'll add another column next to it
in the same ion-row which has no offset but the same size
and there, I'll have my available to label and date time and I'll keep almost the same min and max value,
I'll only increase the min value to the 2nd January because there you have to at least offer it
for one day I guess
and since this is the lowest value here, the lowest value here should be one day
beneath that. Obviously, the December value is equal but you can definitely fine tune this to your requirements.
So now, we have all these controls in place,
the buttons are missing though, right?
Well here, I'll get fancy and I'll add my button in the toolbar. So I'll add ion-buttons here and give
them a slot of primary which should be on the right side of the toolbar on most devices and I'll add
an ion-button in there
which will when clicked trigger onCreateOffer method
and in there, I'll add an ion-icon with a name of checkmark, which is rendering a checkmark icon that
takes the
icon-only slot so that it is styled to give us a nice button that only diplays this icon.
Now let's implement the onCreateOffer method in the Typescript file and for now, I'll just log
creating offered place or something like that.
Now let's have a look at that,
so let's wait for this page to reload and
here we are
and I should probably change the styling where I give every column this red border in the new-offer.page.scss
file.
It certainly will look better without that but with that, that looks pretty good
and you can see if I tap one of these drawers here, I got my date picker where I can select a date unsurprisingly
and all the other inputs here also work as they should and we got this button that correctly calls
this method.
So that is all nice,
now for the logic, how do we handle our inputs here,
how do we let Angular know about them and create a form object?
